recent_posts.title: Issue #77: Swift Is Bigger Than Xcode, a Paste Bug You've Probably Hit, and WWDC Is 57 Days Away
recent_posts.summary: A curated iOS/Swift developer newsletter covering: the Swift VS Code extension now available on Open VSX Registry (enabling Swift in Cursor, VSCodium, and other AI-native IDEs); a workaround for the Xcode 26.4 simulator paste bug using xcrun simctl pbcopy; a reminder that the April 28 App Store SDK deadline requires building with iOS 26 SDK or later; the release of Untold Engine Studio, a Swift/Metal game engine with ECS and Gaussian Splat Rendering; Deep Dish Swift 2026 conference recap; and WWDC 2026 dates (June 8–12).

recent_posts.title: Issue #76: Swift 6.3 Is Here, Swift on Android, Smarter Tests & One Very Important Date
recent_posts.summary: Swift 6.3 released March 24 brings three key improvements to Swift Testing (warning issues, test cancellation, image attachments), the first official Swift SDK for Android enabling cross-platform code sharing with Kotlin/Java apps via Swift Java JNI Core, and the formalized @c attribute for cleaner C interoperability with compile-time signature validation. Xcode 26.3 introduced agentic coding with Claude Agent and OpenAI Codex, supporting full-project reasoning, build execution, and MCP-compatible third-party agents. A reminder that starting April 28, 2026, App Store submissions must target the iOS 26 SDK or later. The 2026 Swift Student Challenge winners were also announced.

recent_posts.title: iOS dev catch-up: Foundation Models tool calling, Swift 6.2 features and SDK deadline
recent_posts.summary: iOS Code Review newsletter issue #75 covers several key updates for iOS developers. Apple's Foundation Models framework now supports tool calling, enabling agentic app features where the on-device model can invoke app-defined tools for real-time data. Swift 6.2 introduces Default Actor Isolation to reduce @MainActor annotation boilerplate, transactional state updates via the new Observations async sequence, and exit testing in Swift Testing for verifying fatal termination conditions. Additional highlights include Swift running in the browser via WebAssembly, the Swift System Metrics 1.0 release for process-level profiling, and a reminder that App Store Connect will require the iOS 26 SDK starting April 28, 2026.

recent_posts.title: iOS Code Review Newsletter - Issue #74
recent_posts.summary: Issue #74 of the iOS Code Review newsletter discusses building the perfect release train for app updates, the new integration between ChatGPT and Xcode, and advanced testing techniques in Swift. The issue covers how to inject parameters into tests, use traits and tags for conditional testing, group tests into suites, and use the #require macro for clearer test prerequisites. Additionally, it highlights leveraging Apple's AI/ML tools for improved user search results on iOS 12 and above.

recent_posts.title: iOS Code Review Newsletter - Issue #73
recent_posts.summary: Issue #73 of the iOS Code Review newsletter features insights into creating custom iOS keyboards with Swift and SwiftUI, using Xcode 16 for Swift Testing, and effective use of the MainActor attribute in Swift 6. The post also discusses customization options for Apple's Writing Tools in iOS 18 and highlights Swift Evolution proposals, upcoming events, and code tips.

recent_posts.title: iOS Code Review Newsletter - Issue #72
recent_posts.summary: This issue of iOS Code Review covers recent highlights including WWDC announcements, Swift 6 features like typed throws, and AI advancements. It delves into efficient mobile release trains, the new @Entry macro in SwiftUI, and presents videos from SwiftCraft UK 2024. Additionally, it announces the release of GitHub Copilot for Xcode and provides tips on improving user privacy in multitasking and requesting expedited app reviews.

recent_posts.title: iOS Code Review - Issue #71
recent_posts.summary: The 71st issue of iOS Code Review introduces a new comment section for registered users. Highlights include Squarespace's method for uneventful releases, an AI Q&A layer for WWDC, contentMargins in SwiftUI from iOS 17, a GitHub repo with Swift Regex examples, and a guide on modular app architecture in SwiftUI.

recent_posts.title: iOS Code Review Newsletter - Issue #70
recent_posts.summary: ISSUE #70: After a long summer break, the iOS Code Review Newsletter returns with insights into type-safe identifiers in Swift, essential guides on Swift Concurrency, a detailed look at SwiftUI format styles, and a spotlight on ButtonKit for async button actions. The author also shares personal updates about joining the startup Lun, which focuses on AR tech in the climate space.

recent_posts.title: iOS Code Review Newsletter - Issue #69
recent_posts.summary: Issue #69 of iOS Code Review features insights and discoveries in iOS development, including the introduction of 'containerRelativeFrame' and 'contentMargins' in iOS 17, as well as a discussion on overrated Swift features. Pragma Conference is also mentioned as the sponsor.

recent_posts.title: iOS Code Review Newsletter - Issue #68
recent_posts.summary: This post discusses the AASA file and its role in enabling iOS features like Universal Links, Shared Web Credentials, Handoff, and App Clips. It also mentions the ContentUnavailableView and provides tips for overcoming obstacles in software engineering. Additionally, it promotes the Swift Craft conference for developers working on Apple platforms.
